bull.b: Repeat purchasing and refill behavior provide evidence that VIZZ can generate recurring demand rather than only initial prescriptions. Stronger persistence in mature cohorts could improve customer lifetime value and support more durable commercial economics as the launch broadens.

A roughly 90% direct product gross-margin target indicates attractive underlying product economics if sales scale. High incremental margins could allow future revenue growth to convert more effectively into gross profit and help absorb the company’s substantial fixed commercial and operating costs.

A growing international partner network and multiple regulatory submissions expand potential access beyond the U.S. launch. This structure can diversify future commercialization opportunities and provide additional licensing or milestone pathways as regional approvals progress.

bear.b: The scale of current operating losses remains disproportionate to revenue, showing that commercialization has not yet reached the level needed to support the cost base. Persistently negative earnings could require continued financing and delay the path to sustainable profitability.

Heavy negative operating and free cash flow indicates that the business is consuming capital while building its commercial platform. Even with cash on hand, continued burn can reduce financial flexibility and increase dependence on external funding before sales scale sufficiently.

Limited retail traction narrows the company’s current distribution footprint and makes it harder to establish recurring demand across the broader eye-care channel. It also leaves commercial performance more dependent on e-pharmacy, limiting channel diversification during the launch phase.
